thesis: ExlService Holdings (Nasdaq: EXLS). Q3 2026 10-Q and release filed 2026-10-27. Q3 revenue 634.0M, +19.7% reported (+19.9% constant currency); Data and AI-led 406.9M (+36.3%, release says 31% organic), Digital operations 227.1M (-1.7%). 9M revenue 1,799.1M (+16.4%). Adjusted EPS Q3 0.62 (+28.5%), GAAP diluted 0.45; adjusted operating margin 19.3% vs 19.4%, GAAP 14.0%. FY26 guide raised: revenue 2.430B to 2.440B (15% organic), adjusted EPS 2.34 to 2.36. TTM (FY25 + 9M26 - 9M25): revenue 2,341.7M, NI 260.6M, OCF 326.2M, capex 55.0M, FCF 271.2M; SBC TTM 93.0M leaves 178.2M. Close 43.60 x 150,788,731 shares (cover 2026-10-23) = market cap 6,574M = 25.2x TTM GAAP NI, 18.6x FY26 adjusted EPS midpoint 2.35; FCF yield 4.1% (2.7% after SBC). Cash 154.1M plus short-term investments 178.6M, borrowings 511.0M (new 1B secured facility Aug 2026), total liabilities 1,145.3M vs 789.5M at year-end; iMerit acquired 2026-06-22 (153.8M net cash). 9M buybacks cash 212.4M.
counterthesis: Growth in Data and AI-led includes acquisitions (31% organic vs 36% reported), and the legacy Digital operations line is shrinking; AI-driven automation could cut revenue per task in the BPO base. Debt rose about 217M in 2026 while buybacks consumed 212M, so shareholder returns are partly debt funded. GAAP operating margin 14.0% sits well below adjusted 19.3%; SBC is 93M TTM. Stock is up about 7% since earnings (40.93 on 10-27). Rupee (INR guide 95) and wage inflation are margin risks. Customer concentration: no customer above 10%, a strength.
invalidation: Fails if organic Data and AI-led growth decelerates sharply, AI substitution erodes Digital operations faster, margins compress, or leverage from acquisitions and buybacks constrains flexibility.
